plan.title: KO x drug interaction in brain bulk RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is a genotype x treatment interaction on a balanced 2x2 design with 4 replicates per cell (16 samples in metadata.csv; counts.csv holds raw salmon gene-level counts for 12,000 gene symbols across 17 columns, the extra column being the gene symbol key). The plan therefore fits one DESeq2 model with the design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment on the raw counts, with WT and vehicle set explicitly as reference levels, and tests the interaction coefficient with the Wald test. That interaction coefficient is the direct answer; the two simple treatment effects (drug vs vehicle within WT, and within KO) are reported beside it because neither an interaction coefficient nor a simple effect alone answers the question on its own.

Step order: sample-structure QC first (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes) to confirm the four cells separate as expected and that no sample is misassigned or an outlier, since with n=4 per cell one bad sample distorts the interaction badly. Then the DE step: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=4 samples, the smallest cell size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, Wald test, ashr shrinkage (the simple effect in KO is a sum of two coefficients, i.e. a contrast, so apeglm cannot serve it), BH within each contrast with independent filtering at alpha 0.05. A DESeq2/edgeR-QL cross-check on the same design gives a robustness read on the interaction gene set. Enrichment runs preranked (fgsea on the Wald statistic, full tested list, sets of 15-500 genes) once per contrast against human MSigDB Hallmark and then WikiPathways human, both present in the reference store; the enrichment is deliberately preranked rather than over-representation because an interaction contrast at n=4 per cell typically yields a short significant list.

Power caveat carried through the whole plan: an interaction coefficient is a difference of differences and carries roughly twice the variance of a simple effect, so at 4 replicates per cell power is low. A null interaction result is not evidence that the drug acts identically in both genotypes, and the report must say so explicitly rather than presenting the simple effects as if they settled the question.

DESeq2 Wald test on the genotype:treatment interaction coefficient plus the two simple treatment effects
Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate with independent filtering
fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic with MSigDB Hallmark, then WikiPathways human
Interaction report: simple effects and interaction contrast side by side, MA and dispersion plots, session info

Hallmark and WikiPathways results are reported in separate tables per contrast, never pooled, with the release/version of each collection stated
Leading-edge genes with their Wald statistics are listed per significant set, and overlapping leading edges between reported sets are marked
The share of tested genes not matched to the collection identifier space is reported
A fixed random seed is set and reported for the fgsea permutations
constraints: Use the human pathway gene-set collections only (samples are Homo sapiens, taxon 9606) — a mouse or rat collection here would be an error
Do not threshold the ranked list before the test, and do not run an over-representation test in place of the ranked test
Keep the two collections in separate result tables; a pathway present in both is one finding tested twice, not two findings
Collapse redundant significant sets before reporting and keep the full table as a supplement
Set and report the permutation seed
caveats: If the human hallmark or WikiPathways collection cannot be resolved in the environment at run time, report which collection was unavailable and continue with the one that resolved; the enrichment is interpretive support, not the answer to the research question
Enrichment results are method-dependent — present a significant set as a hypothesis for follow-up, not as an established mechanism
An enriched pathway on the interaction ranking means the drug's transcriptional effect on that pathway differs between genotypes, not that the pathway is up or down in either arm on its own

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea on the full tested list is the default enrichment (R-0107); human hallmark first then WikiPathways from the store (R-0048, R-0165); one run per contrast (R-0104); disputed ranking metric resolved in favour of the Wald stat and stated (R-0108, R-0099).

steps.name: Interaction report
steps.question: Taken together, does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — and with what confidence, given 4 replicates per cell?
steps.description: Assemble the final report. Give the three results side by side per gene: the drug-vs-vehicle effect in WT (reference genotype), the drug-vs-vehicle effect in KO, and the interaction contrast that is the difference between them, with the reference levels (WT, vehicle) named beside the tables. Carry the unshrunken log2FoldChange, its lfcSE, and the ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange for each gene; rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken value. Include the MA plot and the dispersion plot from the DESeq2 fit before the gene tables, and the p-value histogram per contrast. Report the DESeq2/edgeR overlap from T1S3 as the robustness statement with the intersection as the high-confidence interaction set. Report the enrichment per contrast per collection with the database, its release, the ranking metric (Wald stat), the universe (tested genes), the size window, and the leading edges. State the method, package versions, the design formula, every contrast, the thresholds, the number of genes tested, and the number of DE genes per contrast, plus sessionInfo and the seeds. State plainly the power limitation: with 4 replicates per cell the interaction coefficient is a difference of differences with a large standard error, so a small or empty interaction list does not establish that the drug acts the same way in both genotypes.
steps.context: The synthesis step for the research question. Its central obligation is to keep the interaction contrast, not the pair of simple effects, as the answer — and to be honest about how much this design can resolve.
acceptance_criteria: A per-gene table gives the WT simple effect, the KO simple effect, and the interaction contrast side by side, with the reference levels WT and vehicle named
Unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE and ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange are all present; ranking and plots use the shrunken value
MA plot and dispersion plot from the DESeq2 fit, and the per-contrast p-value histograms, appear before the gene tables
DESeq2 vs edgeR overlap is reported and the intersection named as the high-confidence interaction set
Enrichment reporting names each collection with its release, the Wald-stat ranking metric, the tested-gene universe, the 15-500 size window, and the leading-edge genes per significant set
Method, package versions, design formula, all contrasts, thresholds, n tested, n DE per contrast, sessionInfo and all seeds are recorded with the results
An explicit statement of the interaction power limitation at n=4 per cell appears in the conclusions
constraints: Do not present a gene significant in one simple effect and not the other as evidence of a differential drug effect — only the interaction contrast supports that claim
Do not report the union of DESeq2 and edgeR calls as the result
State the number of significantly changed genes per contrast, including when it is zero
Enrichment findings are stated as hypotheses for follow-up, with the method dependence noted
caveats: If the interaction list is empty, the correct conclusion is that this design did not detect a genotype-dependent drug effect at FDR 0.05, not that none exists
Any sensitivity refit (e.g. excluding a QC-flagged sample) must be reported beside the primary result, never in place of it

grounding.reason: Interaction design reporting: simple effects and interaction contrast side by side with the reference levels named (R-0092), shrunken and unshrunken effects (R-0085), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), full reproducibility record (R-0041, R-0086).
